idiom_name: conditional Akka Streams Flow.via splice / Function1.andThen
implementation_notes: In Akka Streams the route is a linear chain of Source/Flow/Sink operators, so the detour is a stage spliced in conditionally: val route = if (cfg.detourEnabled) base.via(auditFlow) else base, with both branches wired to the same Source and Sink, i.e. the same destination. Where no stream library is involved, Scala's own composition does the job: val f = if (cfg.detourEnabled) base.andThen(audit) else base, which is the same Detour with the toggle resolved at wiring time. Keep the detour stage a single Flow so the graph remains linear and fusion/naming behaviour stays predictable.
code_sketch:
val base  = Flow[Order]
val audit = Flow[Order].map(auditService.tag)      // inspect / modify
val route = if (cfg.detourEnabled) base.via(audit) else base

Source(orders).via(route).runWith(Sink.foreach(orderService.handle))
pitfalls: Splicing a stage changes graph shape, names and async boundaries, so logging and stage attributes shift whenever the detour is switched on.
A detour stage that fans out (Broadcast/Balance) is no longer a single destination path and changes delivery semantics - the rejoin must stay one-to-one.
A stream graph is materialised once: a live toggle has to be a branch/filter inside the graph (or a restart), not a different graph.
